newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Dates proposed for 1998 WTO ministers' meeting.
newsitem.headline: Dates proposed for 1998 WTO ministers' meeting.

text.p: Member countries of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) agreed on Thursday to consider dates next February or May for the holding of the body's second Ministerial Meeting, trade officials said.
Delegations to the WTO's monthly General Council meeting heard a proposal from Canada that the meeting, the organisation's highest authority, be held on February 2-4 or May 18-20.

No immediate decision was taken, but the officials said member countries agreed the meeting would be preceded by celebrations of the 50th anniversary of the founding of the WTO's predecessor, the GATT, which falls next year.
GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) was absorbed into the WTO from January 1995 under accords reached in the 1986-93 Uruguay Round of world trade negotiations.

Cuba, where the international conference which led to creation of the GATT was held in 1948, is itself planning to hold an international seminar near the end of this year to study how the trade system has helped developing countries.
A Cuban official reminded the Council on Thursday of these plans, although no formal date has yet been set.

Trade officials said it was not yet clear if Havana -- under economic boycott by the United States for nearly four decades -- would be inviting trade ministers or top WTO officials, including Director-General Renato Ruggiero.

The communist-ruled island has been the focus of a major dispute in the WTO between the United States and the European Union -- now temporarily shelved -- over the Helms-Burton law aimed at limiting foreign investment in Cuba.
But the law has been fiercely criticised by other major U.S. trading partners, including Canada and Mexico, as well as all Latin American countries.
